# Changelog

All notable changes to PerMark are documented here. The format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and the project uses [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).

## [Unreleased]

### Editing (Source mode)
- **Edit** a Markdown document (`E`, Ctrl+E or the Edit button) in a source editor with Markdown highlighting, line numbers and soft wrap at the reading
  width; **Ctrl+S** saves, **Done**, Ctrl+E or Esc goes back to reading. PerMark writes the text as you typed it and keeps the file's BOM and line
  endings: lines you did not touch keep their own bytes, also in a file that mixes CRLF, LF and a lone CR, and a save without an edit writes the very same
  file. Saving keeps the file's permissions. The editor is loaded only when you start editing. Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I, Ctrl+K, Ctrl+` and Ctrl+Shift+X wrap the selection in Markdown.
- Unsaved work is never lost quietly: an `Unsaved` mark in the header, a dot on the file in the tree and a `*` in the window title; leaving the document
  (closing the window, or **Restart to update**) while it has unsaved changes asks to Save, Discard or Keep editing, and Follow never jumps away while you edit.
- If someone else (an agent, another editor) changes the file while you edit, a clean buffer reloads in place and a buffer with your edits shows a banner:
  **Reload theirs** or **Keep mine**; a file deleted meanwhile can be saved again or discarded. A save never overwrites a version you have not seen: the file is compared once more right before it is replaced, so
  an agent that saves while your save is being written makes it a conflict. A save
  that fails (read-only file, access denied) keeps your text and offers Retry and Copy all.
- Your own saves are not news: no glow, toast, feed entry or Follow jump for what you just wrote, while the search index and the git badge still catch up.
- **Ctrl+N** creates a new Markdown file: type its name in the tree (`.md` is added), and it opens for editing with the caret after the title. Pasting or
  dropping an image into the editor saves it next to the document in `assets/` and inserts the link.
- Visual (WYSIWYG) editing is next; its switch is in the header, disabled for now. Files that are binary, over 5 MB, not Markdown or not UTF-8 cannot be edited
  (the Edit button says why). "Open in external editor" moved to the `...` menu.

### Outline
- The right panel has two tabs, **Changes** (the live feed and "Since last visit", as before) and **Outline**. The Outline lists the
  open document's headings, indented by nesting; the section you are reading is marked and the list follows you as you scroll.
  Click or press Enter on a heading to jump to it (it is tinted for a moment); Left and Right collapse and expand a section, and
  the collapsed state is kept per document while the app is open, even when the document is rewritten under you.
- When an agent rewrites the document, a dot marks the sections whose blocks changed (a collapsed section shows it when something
  inside it changed), and goes away with the change bars. A dot on the Changes tab says the feed moved while you were on the Outline.
- **Ctrl+Alt+O** shows the Outline (opening the panel if it is collapsed); press it again to go back to the previous tab. In
  Simple mode it opens the outline as a popover under the header. Long documents show the first 1,000 headings.
- The tab you were on is remembered per project.

### Reading width
- Three reading widths instead of two: **Comfortable** (760 px, the default), **Wide** (1100 px) and **Full** (the whole document
  pane). One click on the status bar width button, the menu entry or Ctrl+Alt+W moves to the next; Settings has all three. The
  width is remembered per project, and a project that used the old "Wide" setting keeps it.
- Tables, code blocks, Mermaid diagrams, display formulas and wide images take the room they need, up to the pane, while the text
  stays at the comfortable measure. A narrow table or a short snippet stays where it was; glow, change bars and find highlights
  follow the block.

### Explorer follows the open file
- Whatever opens a document (Quick open, search, a link, the feed, Follow, back and forward, the restored session), the Explorer
  opens the folders above it, selects it and scrolls it into view by the shortest way, without taking the keyboard focus. Worktree
  files appear under their worktree, and a file the filter hides is shown dimmed while it is open.
- **Always select the opened file** (Explorer `[:]` menu, on by default) turns it off; "Reveal open doc" still works.

### Explorer filter
- A filter in the Explorer header chooses what the tree shows: Documents, Docs and assets (the default), Everything, or Custom
  (file-type checkboxes plus optional `+pattern` / `-pattern` globs such as `+*.sql -archive/**`). Folders with no visible file are
  hidden, so a code repository shows `docs/` and the root documents instead of every source folder.
- "Only assets next to documents" (on by default) keeps the JSON, TOML, YAML, XML and image files of code folders out of the
  tree: such a file shows only when its folder, or the one above it, holds a document.
- The tree footer says how many files are hidden ("Showing 52 of 1,204 files") and offers **Show all** for the moment. A hidden file
  you open by link, search, Ctrl+P or the feed stays in the tree, dimmed, while it is open.
- Quick open follows the same filter and ends with "+N hidden files match", which lists them.
- Your choice is remembered per project. A project can set the default for everyone in `.permark/config.toml`
  (`[tree] show = "docs-and-assets"`, `include = [...]`, `exclude = [...]`); your own choice wins.

### Tags and descriptions
- Tag any file and give it a one-line description. Tags written in a document's frontmatter (`tags:`) are read automatically and
  shown with a file glyph; tags added in the app are kept outside your files, in `.permark/meta.toml` once the project is
  initialized (committable, so teammates and agents can read it) or in the app's own storage before that.
- A strip at the top of the document shows the description and the tags; `T` (or the menu) edits them, with autocomplete.
- A Tags view (`Ctrl+Shift+T`) lists every tag with its number of files; pick one, or Ctrl+click several, to list the files.
- `tag:name` filters in Quick open and in Search; descriptions show in the tree tooltip, Quick open and search results.
- Renamed files keep their tags; entries of deleted files are kept until you choose "Clean up".
- A `meta.toml` that cannot be read (for example a merge conflict) makes the app's tags read-only and says which line is wrong.

## [0.1.0] - 2026-10-14

The first public release.

### Reading
- GitHub-flavored Markdown with tables, task lists, footnotes, alerts and description lists; Mermaid diagrams, KaTeX math,
  syntax highlighting, a frontmatter card, safe embedded HTML, and Unicode-safe heading anchors.
- JSON, XML and plain-text views; binary and very large files are detected; UTF-8 with BOM, UTF-16 and CRLF are handled.
- Light, dark and system themes; zoom; normal or wide reading width; collapsible and resizable side panels.

### Navigation
- IDE mode for folders (file tree that respects `.gitignore`, with git badges) and Simple mode for single files.
- In-app links and anchors with back and forward; images from the vault; external links open in the browser.
- Quick open (`Ctrl+P`), find in page (`Ctrl+F`), recent projects, and session restore.

### Following agents live
- Live reload that keeps your scroll position; changed blocks glow, and removed blocks leave an expandable marker. `F7` jumps between changes.
- A live changes feed with one entry per file, grouped bursts, git operations collapsed into one entry, a "Docs only" filter, and a toast.
- Follow mode opens the document being written (rate-limited).
- "Since last visit" shows what changed while PerMark was closed, even after commits.
- Linked git worktrees are discovered and watched.

### Search
- Section-level full-text search (`Ctrl+Shift+F`): `file › heading › snippet` results that jump to the exact section.

### Git
- Status against a baseline of your last visit (the default) or HEAD; a repo-state banner; clear errors.

### Closing the loop
- Copy path, copy reference (template, default `@{path}`), and copy selection with reference.
- Open in your default app, and show in the file manager.

### Project
- Optional `.permark/` project folder for shared settings; zero footprint by default.
- In-app updates through GitHub Releases, with signed update packages.

# Contributing to PerMark

Thanks for your interest. PerMark is created and maintained by Edelmar Schneider, who sets its direction and has
the final say on what gets merged. Issues, ideas and pull requests are welcome.

## Before you start
- For anything bigger than a small fix, open an issue first so we can agree on the approach.
- The product is tool-agnostic: features rely on the file system and git, never on one specific AI tool.
- Every user-facing string goes through `src/lib/i18n/`. Code, docs and commit messages are in English.

## Workflow
- git-flow: branch from `develop` (`feature/<name>`), and open the pull request against `develop`.
- Conventional Commits: `feat(render): ...`, `fix(watch): ...`, `docs: ...`.
- The quality gate must pass:

```bash
npm run check   # rustfmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test, svelte-check, vitest
```

The editor's round-trip test keeps the block ranges that the Rust parser finds in a frozen snapshot of the project's documents
(`src/lib/editor/corpus/docs/`), so editing the README or the changelog never affects it. When you change the block parser, `npm run check` says the
ranges in `src/lib/editor/corpus/` are stale; regenerate them with:

```bash
UPDATE_CORPUS=1 npx vitest run src/lib/editor/corpus.test.ts
UPDATE_CORPUS=1 cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml corpus
```

(In PowerShell, set the variable first: `$env:UPDATE_CORPUS = "1"`.)

To refresh the snapshot on purpose (for example to cover new Markdown the project's documents now use), copy the current files over it and regenerate:

```bash
cp README.md CHANGELOG.md CONTRIBUTING.md src/lib/editor/corpus/docs/
cp docs/design/*.md src/lib/editor/corpus/docs/design/
```

## Sign your commits (DCO)
By contributing you certify the [Developer Certificate of Origin](https://developercertificate.org/): that you wrote
the change, or otherwise have the right to submit it under the project's licenses. Add a sign-off line to each commit:

```bash
git commit -s -m "fix(links): decode %20 in anchors"
```

which appends `Signed-off-by: Your Name <you@example.com>`.

## Licensing of contributions
Unless you state otherwise, any contribution you submit is licensed under both [MIT](LICENSE-MIT) and
[Apache-2.0](LICENSE-APACHE), the same as the project, without additional terms. The PerMark name and logo are covered
by [TRADEMARKS.md](TRADEMARKS.md).

# PerMark **A fast, beautiful Markdown IDE that keeps up with your AI agents.** Created and maintained by [Edelmar Schneider](https://github.com/EdelmarSchneider). Open a folder and read it like a wiki. Watch documents change live as agents write them, see exactly what changed, and find any section in seconds. It works with any AI tool, or with none. [Features](#features) · [Install](#install) · [Usage](#usage) · [Shortcuts](#keyboard-shortcuts) · [Roadmap](#roadmap) · [Contributing](#contributing)
--- ## Why PerMark? AI coding agents write a lot of Markdown: specs, plans, research notes, reports. Reading that as raw text in a terminal or an editor is tiring. Browser extensions render one file at a time and don't show what changed. PerMark closes the gap between **the documents your agents produce** and **you**, the human who has to read, check and steer them. - **Read** beautifully rendered Markdown, with Mermaid, math, alerts, footnotes and frontmatter. - **Navigate** a whole folder like a local wiki: relative links, back and forward, quick open. - **Follow** agents live: changed blocks glow, removed blocks leave a marker, and a live feed shows every file being touched. - **Review** what happened since your last visit, even if the agent already committed. - **Find** "character descriptions" or "retry policy" across hundreds of long docs, down to the exact section. PerMark only relies on your **filesystem and git**. It works the same with Claude Code, opencode, Cursor, Aider, Codex or Gemini CLI, and it's a great Markdown reader if you don't use AI at all. ## Features ### 📖 Reading that feels like a book - GitHub-flavored Markdown: tables, task lists, footnotes, alerts (`> [!NOTE]`), description lists - **Mermaid** diagrams, **KaTeX** math, syntax-highlighted code with copy buttons - Frontmatter shown as a clean metadata card - Light and dark themes, adjustable zoom and reading width, a focus mode with both side panels collapsed - JSON, XML and plain text through an extensible renderer registry ### 🧭 Navigate like a wiki - Open a **folder** for IDE mode (tree, search, live feed) or a **single file** for a distraction-free reader - Relative links, anchors and images resolve inside the app, with back and forward history - Quick open (`Ctrl+P`), find in page (`Ctrl+F`), session restore and recent projects - One process per project: `permark ~/code/my-project` ### ⚡ Follow your agents live - Documents reload **without losing your scroll position** - **Changed blocks glow** and fade; **removed blocks leave a marker** you can expand - **Live changes** feed: one entry per file, bursts grouped, `git checkout` storms collapsed into one line - **Follow mode** automatically opens the doc the agent is writing (rate-limited, never jumps while you're selecting) - Git worktrees are discovered automatically, so changes made by agents working in parallel branches show up too ### 🔍 Find anything, to the section - Section-level full-text search (`Ctrl+Shift+F`): results show `file › heading › snippet` and jump to the exact spot - Accent- and case-insensitive, with light stemming, and incremental updates as files change - Semantic search with a local multilingual model is planned for v0.3 (see the [roadmap](#roadmap)) ![Section search: "character descriptions" finds characters.md › Aria](docs/assets/screenshot-search.png) ### 🌿 Git-aware - Badges for modified, added and untracked files, with folder roll-up - Baseline **"since your last visit"** (default) or **"since HEAD"**: useful when agents commit every few minutes - Banner for rebase or merge in progress; clear messages when git can't read a repo ### 🔁 Close the loop with your AI - **Copy reference** (`@docs/plan.md`) and **copy selection with reference**: a quoted excerpt plus path and section, ready to paste into any AI chat or CLI - Configurable reference template ### 🗂️ Zero footprint by default PerMark keeps its state in your user profile. If you want settings to travel with the project, run **Initialize PerMark in this project** to create a `.permark/` folder (shared `config.toml`; caches are gitignored automatically). ## Install > Prebuilt installers for Windows, macOS and Linux are published on the [Releases](../../releases) page. > PerMark updates itself: when a new version is out, you'll be offered a one-click restart to update. **Build from source** (requires [Rust](https://rustup.rs), [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 20+ and the [Tauri prerequisites](https://v2.tauri.app/start/prerequisites/)): ```bash git clone https://github.com/EdelmarSchneider/permark.git cd permark npm install npm run tauri build ``` ## Usage ```bash permark # welcome screen with recent projects permark . # open the current folder in IDE mode permark docs/plan.md # open a single file in simple mode ``` You can also drag and drop a folder or a `.md` file onto the window. ## Keyboard shortcuts | Action | Shortcut | |---|---| | Quick open file | `Ctrl+P` | | Search all docs (by section) | `Ctrl+Shift+F` | | Find in page | `Ctrl+F` | | Toggle left / right panel | `Ctrl+B` / `Ctrl+Alt+B` | | Next / previous change | `F7` / `Shift+F7` | | Back / forward | `Alt+←` / `Alt+→` | | Copy reference (or selection with reference) | `Ctrl+Alt+C` | | Zoom in / out / reset | `Ctrl+=` / `Ctrl+-` / `Ctrl+0` | ## Roadmap **v0.2** - File tags and short descriptions ("Character sheets", "NPC dialogues"…): read from frontmatter or added in the app without touching your files, with a Tags view and `tag:` search filters - WYSIWYG editing (tables, images, formatting) with conflict-safe saving that never silently reformats agent-written files - Outline panel, "unread since last read" markers, commit timeline, rendered diff against the baseline - Rich JSON and XML views, clickable code references (`src/main.rs:42`) - Installers with `permark` on `PATH` and `.md` file association **v0.3** - Semantic and hybrid search with a local multilingual embedding model (optional download) **Later** - Review comments that turn into a prompt or a `REVIEW.md` for your agent - An MCP server so any agent can ask PerMark "where is X described?" - Image management, templates, backlinks and `[[wikilinks]]`, export to PDF and HTML ## Tech PerMark is a [Tauri 2](https://v2.tauri.app) app. The core is written in **Rust**: rendering (comrak + ammonia), file watching (notify), git (libgit2) and the search index. The UI is **Svelte 5** + TypeScript running in the system webview. That keeps the installer small and memory use low compared to Electron apps. ## Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome. The project uses **git-flow** (`develop` for integration, `feature/*` branches) and a strict quality gate: ```bash npm run check # rustfmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test, svelte-check, vitest ``` Design and planning docs are in [`docs/`](docs/). See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request. ## License Copyright (c) 2026 Edelmar Schneider. Licensed under either of [MIT](LICENSE-MIT) or [Apache-2.0](LICENSE-APACHE), at your option. "PerMark" and its logo are trademarks of Edelmar Schneider: forks are welcome under a different name. See [TRADEMARKS.md](TRADEMARKS.md).

# PerMark v0.2: design addendum Extends `wireframes.md` (MVP). Same legend, tokens, Lucide icons; all strings via `t()` (keys in §10). New legend: `{tag}` app tag chip, `{tag}f` tag from frontmatter (locked), `*` unread dot, `|~` unsaved-block bar, `[Visual|Source]` segmented switch. Scope order: tags, outline, editing, unread, code refs, commits. ## 0. What changes in the existing shell - **Activity bar**: `[F]` Explorer, `[S]` Search, **`[#]` Tags (new)**, `[L]` right panel, `[T]`, `[*]`. - **Right panel header** gets the segmented switch reserved in the MVP: `Changes | Outline | Commits`. Changes = today's Live changes + Since last visit. A 6px accent dot on `Changes` when events arrive while another tab is shown (same rule as the activity-bar dot). Tab choice persists per project. - **Doc header**: the `[E]` slot becomes `[Edit]` (text button). "Open in external editor" moves to the `[:]` menu (Ctrl+Shift+E unchanged). New `[:]` items: Edit tags and description (T), Images in this doc, Mark as unread. - **Doc meta strip** (new): one quiet row at the top of the reading column, above the frontmatter card, scrolls with the doc. Holds the description and tag chips. Hidden when the doc has neither (then `T` or the menu opens the editor). ## 1. Tags and descriptions (hybrid) ``` +---+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+ |[F]| <- -> docs / specs / live-feed.md M saved 12s ago [@] [Edit] [:] | |[S]|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| |[#]| How the live feed groups watcher events into rows. (description, muted) | |[L]| {feed}f {watcher}f {spec} {needs-review} [+] | | | +--------------------------------------------+ | | | | status: draft updated: 2026-10-13 | (frontmatter card; `tags:` moved to the strip) | | | +--------------------------------------------+ | | | Live changes feed | ``` **Chips**. App tags: 10% tint background + 6px color dot, text in `--text`. File tags: same look plus a Lucide `file-text` glyph at 12px and tooltip "From the file's frontmatter. Edit the file to change it." The same tag in both places shows once, as a file tag. Click a chip = open the Tags view filtered by that tag. `[+]` opens the popover. **Colors**: 8 muted hues (no accent, no git colors), picked by a stable hash of the tag name, so every machine and every teammate sees the same color. No color picker in v0.2. **Popover** (from `[+]`, a chip's context menu, the `[:]` menu, or `T` while reading): ``` +--------------------------------------------------------+ | Description | | [How the live feed groups watcher events._ ] 47/120 | | Tags | | {feed}f {watcher}f {spec x} {needs-review x} [wat_ ] | | +------------------------------------------+ | | | watcher-api 4 files | | | | Create tag "wat" | | | +------------------------------------------+ | | Saved in PerMark, not in the file. [Done] | +--------------------------------------------------------+ ``` - Edits apply immediately (metadata is not the document; no save step). Done or Esc closes. Enter or comma adds the typed/highlighted tag; Backspace on an empty input removes the last app tag; file tags have no `x`. - Autocomplete: existing tags (app + file) fuzzy-matched, ranked by file count; last row "Create tag "x"". - Normalization: trimmed, lowercased, inner spaces become `-`, max 40 chars; `/` is allowed text (no nesting yet). Description: one line, 120 chars, newlines stripped. - The footer names the store; with `.permark/`: "Saved in .permark/meta.toml (shared with the project)." - Works for any file type, including binary and too-large states (the strip sits above the notice). **Storage**. `.permark/meta.toml` when initialized (committable, so teams and agents can read it), else AppData per project. Keyed by vault-relative path: `[files."docs/specs/live-feed.md"] tags = [...] description = "..."`. A `renamed` change moves the entry; entries of missing files are kept (a checkout may restore them) until Clean up. Writes are debounced 300ms and ignored by the watcher; initializing `.permark/` moves the AppData metadata there. **Tags view** (`[#]`, Ctrl+Shift+T): ``` +------------------------------------+ +------------------------------------+ | TAGS [Any|All] | | TAGS | | [filter tags_ ] | | | | [x] (o) spec 12 | | No tags yet. | | [x] (o) needs-review 3 | | Press T on a doc to tag it, or | | [ ] (o) feed (file) 5 | | add `tags:` to its frontmatter. | | [ ] (o) watcher 4 | | | | Untagged 212 | | | |------------------------------------| +------------------------------------+ | 2 FILES spec + needs-review | | * live-feed.md docs/specs | | How the live feed groups... | | plan.md (root) | |------------------------------------| | 3 missing-file entries [Clean up] | +------------------------------------+ ``` - Tag list sorted by count; "(file)" marks tags that exist only in frontmatter. Click a tag = select only it; Ctrl+click or Space = toggle (multi-select). `Any|All` sets OR/AND (default All). Untagged is a pseudo-tag. - File list below: name, folder, description as a muted second line, unread dot, git badge. Click/Enter opens. - Tag context menu: Rename tag..., Remove from all files (app tags only; file tags show these disabled with the "Edit the file to change it" hint). Rename into an existing tag merges, after a confirm with the file count. - States: no tags (above); filter with no match "No tags match 'x'"; selection with no files "No file has all of these tags. Try Any."; `meta.toml` unreadable (e.g. merge conflict): banner "Can't read .permark/meta.toml (line 12). App tags are read-only until it is fixed. [Open file]", file tags still listed. **`tag:` filter** in Search (Ctrl+Shift+F) and Quick open (Ctrl+P): `tag:spec` tokens (AND when repeated) filter results; the rest of the query searches as before. Typing `tag:` opens the same tag autocomplete inline. In Ctrl+P a query that is only `tag:x` lists every file with that tag, sorted by recency. A matched tag renders as a chip in the input row. Unknown tag: "No tag 'x'. Tags: spec, feed, watcher...". **Descriptions show** in: the tree tooltip (path, description, tags), the Quick open row (muted second line, also matched by fuzzy at the lowest rank), and the Search file-group header (muted subline). ## 2. Outline (right panel, `Outline` tab) ``` +---------------------------------+ | Changes [Outline] Commits [>]| | Depth: [2] [3] [All] | |---------------------------------| | v Live changes feed | | Event model o | o = section has a live-changed block | | Grouping | | = current section (accent-muted bar, semibold) | > Rollout | | > Appendix | +---------------------------------+ ``` - Built from the rendered doc's headings (`data-sourcepos`), h1-h6, indented 12px per level. Depth default 3. - **Current section**: the last heading above the top-third line of the viewport; updates on scroll (rAF-throttled); the outline auto-scrolls to keep it visible. - Click/Enter: scroll the heading to the top (8px offset), 1.5s `--mark` tint like a search hit; no history entry. Left/Right collapse/expand; chevrons per node; collapse state is per doc for the session only. - Live reload rebuilds the outline keeping collapse state by heading text; a dot `o` (accent) marks sections whose blocks changed, cleared with the gutter bars. In edit mode it rebuilds 300ms after typing stops. - Ctrl+Alt+O: show the Outline tab (opens the right panel if collapsed); pressed again, returns to the previous tab. - Simple mode has no right panel: Ctrl+Alt+O opens the outline as a popover anchored to the header (same list). - States: no headings "This document has no headings."; non-Markdown "Outline is available for Markdown documents."; no doc "Open a document to see its outline."; more than 1,000 headings: first 1,000 + "Showing 1,000 of 1,312". ### Implementation notes: Outline (2026-10-14, `feature/outline`) - Built as specified with the Decisions applied: **no depth control** and **no Commits tab**, so the switch is `Changes | Outline`. The views are one list (`RIGHT_TABS` in `rightPanel.ts`), so a third tab is one entry there plus its panel. The header is the tabs and the collapse button; the live status and the "Docs only" chip moved to a row under the tabs, in the Changes view (the title "Live changes" is gone: the tab says it). The tabs are a WAI-ARIA tab list (Left/Right move between them). - Pure logic in `outline.ts` (tested): `buildOutline` turns the top-level blocks into the tree, `visibleRows`/`visibleAncestor` apply the collapse state, `currentHeading` finds the section being read, `navigate` is the keyboard, `CollapseMemory` keeps the collapse state. `DocView` reads the DOM (`dom/outlineDom.ts`) after **every** render, fresh or live, and reports to the `outline` store; the panel and the popover only show it (`OutlineList.svelte`, one component for both). - Only **top-level** headings count (not one inside a list item or a quote), the same blocks the block diff and "copy with reference" use. The indent is 12 px per **nesting level**, not per heading level: a document that starts at h2, or skips from h2 to h4, is not indented by the gap. - **Current section**: a binary search over the heading tops at the top-third line, once per animation frame, so a 1,000-heading document costs about ten measurements per frame. Two refinements to "the last heading above the line": at the very bottom of the page the last heading that is on screen counts (it can never reach the line), and a heading chosen in the outline stays current until the reader scrolls by hand (near the end of the page it cannot reach the top, so the scroll alone would highlight its neighbour). When a collapsed heading hides the current one, the collapsed heading carries the bar. - Click or Enter scrolls the heading to 8 px under the top and tints **the heading only** for 1.5 s (a search hit also tints the paragraph after it); it calls DocView directly, so there is no history entry. Focus stays in the list so the next key works. - Collapse state is per document for the session (`CollapseMemory`, the last 64 documents), keyed by heading text; a text that repeats is numbered by order (so the first one keeps its plain key). A renamed heading starts open again. - The accent dot: the blocks of a section that carry `.tm-changed` or a removed-blocks marker, so it lives exactly as long as the gutter bars (the next render replaces both). A **collapsed** heading shows the dot too when something below it changed, so it is not lost by collapsing. - Ctrl+Alt+O (`toggleOutline` in `rightPanel.ts`): opens the panel on the Outline and moves the focus into the list; pressed again it returns to the tab that was showing before and puts the focus on the document (the list it was in is gone). The way back is not saved. The dot on `Changes` follows the activity-bar rule (a document changed), and is set whether the panel is open or collapsed. - Session field `rightTab` (`"changes" | "outline"`, per project). Rust keeps it as an enum that reads an unknown or mistyped value (a newer UI wrote it) as `changes`, so the session survives; a save from before the Outline has no field and reads as `changes`. - Simple mode: Ctrl+Alt+O toggles a popover under the header, right-aligned, closed by Esc, by choosing a heading or by the shortcut. Added beyond the spec: an "Outline" entry in the `[:]` menu, **in Simple mode only**, so a mouse user can find it. - Collapse and resize labels, the activity-bar tooltip and the status-bar toggle now say "right panel" instead of "live changes". `live.title` is gone. Commands `document_source`, `parse_blocks`, `save_document`, `create_document`, `write_asset`. - *Blocks.* A block is the run of whole lines of a top-level comrak node, without its line terminator, so the ranges do not depend on how comrak counts columns, tabs or multi-byte characters. Everything between blocks is a separator that the editor keeps as it is: blank lines, the BOM, the final newline and link reference definitions (comrak consumes those, so they are not blocks). Blocks plus separators give the file back byte for byte; a Rust test checks it on every document of this repository, also as CRLF with a BOM, and that nothing a reader sees hides in a separator. comrak moves footnote definitions to the end of the tree, so the nodes are put back in source order. Alerts (`> [!NOTE]`) and description lists are `other` (locked atoms in Visual); a paragraph that is only `$$...$$` and a `math` fence are `math`. A document nested too deeply to parse safely is one `other` block. - *Saving.* `save_document(path, text, expectedHash)` resolves the path in the vault, compares the hash of the bytes on disk with the one the editor started from, and writes with `util::write_atomic_guarded`. A file that changed or vanished answers `Conflict { diskHash | null }` and is not touched. It refuses read-only files, files over 5 MB, non-Markdown files, binary files and files that are not UTF-8 (UTF-16 or Latin-1: saving would change their encoding; `[Edit]` is disabled for them, with the reason). The text is written as sent; saving the text that is already on disk writes nothing. The UI puts the file's BOM and line endings back around the CodeMirror buffer: every line outside the span that changed keeps its own bytes (LF, CRLF, a lone CR, or a mix of them; a save without an edit is byte for byte the same file), and the changed span is written with the file's most common line ending. - *The race with another writer.* Writing takes long enough (a temp file, then `fsync`, often tens of milliseconds) for an agent to save in the middle of it. So the disk is compared with the editor's version twice: at once, to answer a stale save without writing, and again after the temp file is on disk, immediately before it is renamed over the file (and before every retry of the rename). A writer that got in during the flush makes the save a `Conflict` and its work stays. What no operating system lets us close is the gap between that last read and the rename itself ("replace this file only if it still holds these bytes" does not exist): a few microseconds, but a writer landing exactly there is still overwritten (known limit). - *Permissions.* The temp file takes the permissions of the file it replaces, so a private note stays private: the mode bits on Unix, the read-only attribute on Windows. Not carried over (the file is replaced, not rewritten in place): ACLs and ownership, the hidden and system attributes, and hard links (the saved file is a new one). Each write has a temp file of its own (`....part`). - *Our own writes are not news.* `watch::OwnWrites` is told the hash of what is about to be written (saves, new files, images). When the watcher reports a created or modified change whose content hash is that one, the change is dropped from what the UI hears (no feed row, glow, toast or Follow jump) but still reaches the search index, the tags (front matter) and the git worker, so the badge and the index update. A different content at the same path (an agent saving right after us) stays news. An announcement is for the next report of its path only: the first change the watcher reports for that path ends it, whether it matched or not, and a change whose content the watcher could not read (a locked file) is never taken for ours (the hash it remembers for the file is cleared). Announcements also expire after 5 s, so a write the watcher never reports cannot hide a later change that happens to have the same content. - *New file and images.* `create_document` uses `create_new` (it never overwrites; the name is checked for characters, reserved names (also with spaces before the extension: `con .md`) and trailing dots that fail on some system; Markdown extensions only). `write_asset` writes `/assets/` (png, jpg, gif, webp or svg, 32 MB at most), slugifies the name, adds `-2`, `-3` on a clash, re-checks that an `assets` link does not leave the vault, and refuses in Simple mode (the viewer serves only files next to the opened file there). Image names that Windows opens as devices (`nul`, `con`...) get `-image` added. The image travels as base64 in the IPC call; the command refuses text longer than 32 MB of image before decoding it, and the UI refuses a file over 32 MB before reading it. `parse_blocks` returns no blocks for a text over the 5 MB limit. **Block model** (`src/lib/editor/blockModel.ts`, pure). The text is cut on its UTF-8 bytes into blocks and separators. `compose()` keeps the original bytes of untouched blocks and takes new text for the others. One deviation from the plan: a separator is kept whenever the two neighbours were next to each other in the original, whether or not either was edited (the plan said "both untouched"); otherwise "edit one block and only its bytes change" would not hold for a block followed by two blank lines. `matchBlocks()` (the live diff's LCS on exact block text, not on a hash that could collide) gives "Saved, 2 blocks changed" and keeps the caret on the same block after an external reload. Ship in this order, each end to end: tags, outline, editing core (Visual + Source, save, dirty bar, conflict banner with Reload/Keep mine), unread, code refs, the rest. - **Cut first** (in order): commit timeline (§6); Merge button and the side-by-side diff (keep Reload/Keep mine and a plain "Open both in external diff"); templates (blank only); image manager's vault-wide orphan scan (list used images only); link target autocomplete; outline depth control; Tags view Any/All (AND only); tag rename/merge. - **Risks**: Crepe's block-to-sourcepos mapping for nested lists and tables needs round-trip tests on real agent docs before release; if a block can't be mapped, treat it as a locked atom rather than risk rewriting it. ## 12. i18n keys (new) - `tags.*`: title, filter, any, all, untagged, fromFile, fromFileHint, add, popoverTitle, description, descriptionCounter, createTag, savedApp, savedProject, done, empty, emptyHint, noMatch, noFilesAll, missingEntries, cleanUp, rename, removeAll, mergeConfirm, metaUnreadable, openMetaFile, filesCount, unknownTag - `outline.*`: tab, depth, depthAll, empty, notMarkdown, noDoc, truncated. `panel.*`: tabChanges, tabOutline, tabCommits - `edit.*`: edit, done, save, visual, source, unsaved, saved, savedBlocks, firstSaveHint, writingNow, reloaded, unsavedPrompt, discard, keepEditing, saveError, retry, copyAll, disabledBinary, disabledNonMarkdown, editInSource, followPaused, statusMode - `toolbar.*`: blockType, paragraph, heading1..heading4, bold, italic, strike, code, link, bulletList, orderedList, taskList, quote, table, insertTable, rowAbove, rowBelow, colLeft, colRight, deleteRow, deleteCol, deleteTable, codeBlock, language, image, rule, more, slashFilter - `link.*`: text, target, broken, apply, remove. `codeRef.*`: openAt, ambiguous, runError, openSettings - `conflict.*`: changedOnDisk, showDiff, reloadTheirs, keepMine, merge, deletedOnDisk, saveAsNew, reloadConfirm, theirs, yours, unchangedBlocks, show, close - `images.*`: title, used, unused, missing, external, delete, empty, altPrompt, tooLarge, onlyImages, namePrompt - `newFile.*`: newFile, newFolder, placeholder, exists, invalidChars, templatePicker, blank - `unread.*`: markAllRead, markFolderRead, markUnread, showOnlyUnread, allCaughtUp, folderCount, next - `commits.*`: loadMore, docsCount, otherFiles, lastVisit, empty, notRepo, notInTree, copyOid, copySubject - `settings.*`: sectionAppearance, sectionReferences, sectionEditor, sectionImages, scopeYou, scopeProject, editorPreset, editorCommand, editorPreview, editorCustom, editorSystem, unknownPlaceholder, defaultEditMode, assetsFolder, assetsLocation, nextToDoc, vaultRoot, onPaste, pasteAuto, pasteAsk, invalidFolder - `menu.*` (header `[:]`): openExternal, editTags, imagesInDoc, markUnread ## Decisions (2026-10-14, revisit if needed) - **Tag chips are neutral** (no per-tag colors), keeping the design system's "one accent color" rule. Colors may come later as an option. - **Editor shortcuts**: accept the proposed remaps (in the editor, Ctrl+B/Ctrl+K = bold/link; inline code = Ctrl+\`; Ctrl+E always toggles edit mode; Ctrl+Alt+C = code block while editing). - **Cut from v0.2** (moved to later): commit timeline, the Merge button and side-by-side diff (keep Reload theirs / Keep mine + "open in external diff tool" if trivial), templates (blank file only), the vault-wide orphan-image check (per-doc list only), outline depth control, all/any tag matching (all only), tag rename/merge. - **Build order**: tags → outline → core editor (save, unsaved prompt, Reload/Keep mine, images to `assets/`, new file) → unread markers → code references. - **Safety rule for the editor**: a block that can't be mapped to its source bytes is read-only in the editor; we never rewrite what we can't map. ## Implementation notes: tags (2026-10-14, `feature/tags`) - Built as designed with the Decisions applied: neutral chips, AND only, no rename/merge/"remove from all files". - Metadata for files of linked worktrees (`@wt/...`) is not stored (their file tags are still shown); the editor says so. - Simple mode shows the strip read-only (no `[+]`, no `T`, no Tags view). - A description match in Quick open means every typed word appears in the description (ranked after name matches), not a character-order fuzzy match, which was too noisy on 120-character lines. - `tag:` autocomplete in Quick open and Search lists existing tags only (no "Create tag" row there); a finished `tag:x` token becomes a removable chip, and Backspace in an empty box removes the last chip. - `tag:` in Search filters the backend's hits (it asks for up to 200) instead of changing the index query. - Esc in the tag editor closes it at once (it does not first close the suggestion list). ## 13. Explorer filter (added 2026-10-14) Opening a code repository shows every source folder; for reading, the user wants the docs and their companions. ``` EXPLORER [filter Docs and assets v] +--------------------------------------------------+ | (o) Documents .md .markdown .mdx .txt | | (o) Docs and assets + images, JSON, YAML, TOML, | default | XML, CSV | | ( ) Everything | | ( ) Custom... | |--------------------------------------------------| | [x] Only assets next to documents | | [x] Hide folders with no visible files | +--------------------------------------------------+ ... Showing 52 of 1,204 files [Show all] (tree footer, only when something is hidden) ``` - Presets are bundles of categories: Documents, Images, Data (JSON, YAML, TOML, CSV), XML, Text, Other. **Custom** = category checkboxes plus an optional advanced field of globs (`+*.sql`, `-archive/**`). - **Only assets next to documents** (on by default; for Docs and assets and Custom, disabled for Documents and Everything). Images, data and XML files are companions of documents, not of code: `src-tauri/Cargo.toml`, `tauri.conf.json`, `icons/*.png`, `.github/workflows/*.yml` and `.vscode/*.json` have no business in a reading tree. With the rule on, such a file shows only if its own folder, or the folder above it, directly holds a document (Documents or Text category). So `docs/assets/logo.png` shows (`docs/` holds `.md` files) and the root `package.json` shows (the root holds `README.md`), while `src-tauri/` and `.github/workflows/` disappear. The project root counts as a file's own folder only, never as "the folder above": otherwise every first-level code folder would borrow the root's README. Explicit `+pattern` entries still win. - **Hide folders with no visible files** (on by default) is what makes the tree useful in a code repo: `src/` and `src-tauri/` disappear, `docs/` and the root docs stay. Worktree roots follow the same rule. - Nothing becomes unreachable: a hidden file opened by link, search, Ctrl+P or the feed appears in the tree, dimmed, while it is open. The footer always says how much is hidden and offers Show all (a temporary toggle). - Quick open (Ctrl+P) uses the same filter and shows "+N hidden files match" as a last row that reveals them. Section search is Markdown-only already; the feed keeps its own "Docs only" toggle. - The choice persists per project (session state). With `.permark/`, a project default can be committed in `config.toml` (`[tree] show = "docs-and-assets"`, `include = [...]`, `exclude = [...]`); the user's choice wins. - Filtering happens in the UI over the already loaded tree (no Rust walk change); categories map extensions in one shared table (also used by the renderer registry where it overlaps). - i18n keys: `filter.*`: title, documents, docsAndAssets, everything, custom, hideEmptyFolders, showingOf, showAll, hiddenMatches, categoryDocuments, categoryImages, categoryData, categoryXml, categoryText, categoryOther, advanced, advancedHint, invalidGlob. ### Implementation notes: Explorer filter (2026-10-14, `feature/explorer-filter`) - Built as specified. Pure logic in `fileKinds.ts` (extension to category) and `treeFilter.ts` (presets, patterns, pruning); the filter in force is derived in `stores/filter.svelte.ts` from the saved choice, else the project default, else "Docs and assets". - Presets: Documents = the Documents and Text categories; Docs and assets adds Images, Data and XML. Text is `.txt .text .rst .adoc .org`. - Patterns are gitignore-style, case-insensitive, and apply in **Custom** only: no `/` matches a name at any depth, a `/` anchors at the project root, a trailing `/` means a folder's contents, a folder name also covers what is inside it, and the last matching entry wins. `*`, `**`, `?`, `[abc]` and `{a,b}` work. Entries are separated by spaces or commas. In a worktree they match the path inside the worktree. - `[tree]` in `config.toml`: `show` picks the preset (default `docs-and-assets`); `include` and `exclude` become `+` and `-` entries, so a project with patterns opens as **Custom** with the preset's categories checked (every active rule is visible in the popover). `show = "custom"` starts from nothing: only `include` is shown. The config is read when the project opens. - "Show all" is not saved; any change in the popover ends it. While it is on, the footer reads "Showing all N files [Use filter]". - Quick open without a query lists recent files that pass the filter; "+N hidden files match" appears once something is typed and reveals the hidden matches (dimmed) for as long as the palette is open. - **Only assets next to documents** (added after review; `TreeFilter.assetsNearDocs`, default true): the rule above, with `documentFolders()` listing the folders that directly hold a document and `fileTest()` applying it after the category check and before the patterns (so `+pattern` and `-pattern` still win, the last match first). A worktree root is a root: its files are judged against the worktree's own folders. On this repository (258 files) Docs and assets shows 32: the Markdown files, `docs/assets/*`, and the root `package.json`, `package-lock.json` and `tsconfig.json`. Consequence: a project whose images live in a first-level `assets/` folder with no document in it hides them until the box is unchecked or a `+assets/**` pattern is added. - The saved filter is read leniently: a `show` this build does not know (written by a newer UI) reads as the default preset and keeps the rest; a filter that cannot be read at all reads as "none chosen". The session itself is never lost to it. - Added i18n keys beyond the list above: `buttonLabel`, `hint`, `documentsHint`, `docsAndAssetsHint`, `categories`, `categoryDataHint`, `showingAll`, `useFilter`, `hiddenFile`, `noneVisible`, `assetsNearDocs`, `assetsNearDocsHint`. - Not changed: the Rust renderer registry keeps its own format list (the category table is UI-side), and Search, the Tags view and the feed are not filtered. ## 14. "Open with PerMark" in the file manager (added 2026-10-14) - Windows: context-menu entries on folders, on a folder's background (opens the current folder) and on `.md` files (Simple mode). Registered under `HKCU\Software\Classes` (no admin), via NSIS installer hooks (and the WiX fragment for the MSI). On Windows 11 they appear under "Show more options" (the compact menu needs MSIX packaging; later). - **Optional**: an installer checkbox (checked by default) and a Settings toggle ("Show 'Open with PerMark' in the file manager") that adds or removes the entries at runtime. Updates keep the user's choice (the installer hook respects a stored opt-out); uninstall always removes them. - Later: Linux (`.desktop` entry with `inode/directory`), macOS (Finder Quick Action). Build order update: tags → **Explorer filter** → outline → core editor → unread → code refs → **Open with PerMark**. ## 15. Reading width (added 2026-10-14) The reading column was capped at 760 px (`--measure`) or 1100 px (wide). Long text lines tire the eye, but tables, code blocks and diagrams, which AI docs have plenty of, were squeezed. - **Three widths**: Comfortable (760 px, default), Wide (1100 px), **Full** (the whole doc pane, with the usual side padding). The header/settings width control cycles through them; the session stores `width: "comfortable" | "wide" | "full"` (migrating the old `wide: boolean`), per project as today. - **Breakout for wide blocks**: in every width, tables, code blocks, Mermaid diagrams, display math and images wider than the text measure may grow up to the pane width (minus padding), centred on the column; paragraphs, lists, headings and quotes stay at the measure. A block only breaks out when its content needs it (narrow tables stay at the measure). Horizontal scroll inside a block remains only when even the pane is too narrow. - Find highlights, live-change glow, removed-block markers, the meta strip and the frontmatter card follow the text measure; broken-out blocks keep their glow and gutter bar aligned to the block. - i18n: `width.comfortable`, `width.wide`, `width.full`. Build order update: tags → Explorer filter → **reading width** → outline → core editor → unread → code refs → Open with PerMark. ### Implementation notes: reading width (2026-10-14, `feature/reading-width`) - Built as specified. `data-width` on `.main` drives the cap: Comfortable keeps `--measure` (760 px), Wide sets it to `--measure-wide` (1100 px), Full lifts the cap on the article, the meta strip and the loading skeleton. The pure rules (names, the cycle, the migration) are in `readingWidth.ts`. - Session: `width` replaces `wide`. A save from before v0.2 carries `wide`: the UI migrates it (`true` becomes Wide, `false` or nothing becomes Comfortable) and never writes it again. Rust keeps both fields as `Option`s so nothing is lost on the way through: a `width` this build does not know (written by a newer UI) reads as unset, like the Explorer filter, and the session survives. The cycle is one control in three places: the status bar button, the `[:]` menu entry ("Reading width: Wide") and Ctrl+Alt+W (the shortcut is now `cycleWidth`); Settings shows the three as a segmented control. - The breakout is CSS only, with no measuring script. `.doc-column` wraps the article as a size container, so `100cqw` is the pane's content width. A top-level `.table-wrap`, `.code-block`, `.diagram` or `.tm-wide` block is `width: max-content` (what its content needs) between `min-width: 100%` (the text measure) and `max-width: 100cqw` (the pane), centred with `left: 50%; translateX(-50%)`. A webview without container units keeps the text measure. "Needs room" therefore means the content's natural width: a table is as wide as its columns want to be, so a table with long prose cells also takes the pane (and wraps less); a narrow table or a short snippet stays at the measure. - Only top-level blocks break out. A table or code block inside a list item, a quote or `
` keeps scrolling inside its parent. `.tm-wide` marks the paragraph of a lone image (or a linked image) when the block is enhanced, and the paragraph of a lone display formula once KaTeX has rendered it (so the raw TeX never flashes wide). Mermaid draws `width="100%"`, which has no size of its own, so the SVG gets the width of its `viewBox` as a pixel width (still capped at 100% of the figure). - Glow and gutter bar belong to the block's own box, so they move with it; `.tm-removed` markers and `.md-body` paragraphs stay at the measure. Checked in the mock at Comfortable, Wide and Full, light and dark, with both side panels open and collapsed (no sideways page scroll in any), at zoom 70% to 130%, with find highlights and a live save. With both panels open at 1440 px the pane is narrower than the measure, so nothing can break out; collapse a panel to see it. - Unchanged and noticed: a table's gutter bar is clipped by the table's own scroll container (`overflow-x: auto`), as before; its glow is not. - The mock vault has `docs/design/reading-width.md` (a wide table, a long code line, a Mermaid chain, a display formula and a 1000 px image between ordinary paragraphs; each save edits the wide blocks and drops a paragraph). - i18n: `width.comfortable`, `width.wide`, `width.full`, `menu.width`, `status.widthHint`. Removed: `menu.wide`, `status.normalWidth`, `status.wide`, `settings.widthNormal`, `settings.widthWide`. ## 16. Always select the opened file (added 2026-10-14) The Explorer should show where the open document lives, however it was opened, without anyone having to ask. - **When**: a document becomes the open one by any route: Quick open, search, a link, the feed, Follow, back and forward, the restored session, the tree itself. The Explorer opens the folders above it, selects its row and scrolls it into view. - **How it moves**: the least it can. Nothing scrolls when the row is already visible; otherwise the list scrolls by the shortest way (no smooth animation) and only the Explorer's own list moves. Keyboard focus stays where the person is: the tree's cursor moves to the file, but focus does not jump into the tree. - **On by default**, with a checkbox "Always select the opened file" in the Explorer's `[:]` menu, next to "Reveal open doc". Turning it off stops the automatic reveal only; "Reveal open doc" and the breadcrumb folders still work. The choice is the session field `autoReveal` (per project, like the width), and a session without it means on. - **Collapsed left panel**: nothing visible happens, but the folders are open and the row is selected, so opening the panel (or switching back to the Explorer from Search or Tags) shows the file at once. - **Explorer filter**: a file the filter hides is already kept in the tree, dimmed, while it is open (section 13). It is revealed and selected like any other file. - **Worktrees**: a worktree file is revealed under its worktree root, in the Worktrees section, and the section is expanded if it was collapsed (the project's own section is expanded for a project file). - **Not triggered by**: a jump inside the document that is already open (an anchor link, a search hit in it), Simple mode (no Explorer), a failed open. - i18n: `explorer.autoReveal`. ### Implementation notes: always select the opened file (2026-10-14, `feature/reading-width`) - One choke point: `docs.open()` asks the Explorer to reveal on every successful open (the logic that decides is `reveal.ts`: `planReveal` lists the folders to open, outermost first and without the ones already open, and names the section; `shouldAutoReveal` weighs the setting, Simple mode and in-document jumps). Back and forward, which call `docs.open()` directly, are covered; before, only `app.openDoc()` revealed, so back and forward did not. - A request that opens the file that is already open (Ctrl+P on it, a tree click) still reveals, so the tree comes back to it after being collapsed or scrolled away. - `Tree.svelte` applies the reveal: it moves the tree cursor and scrolls the list with `nearestScrollTop` instead of `scrollIntoView` (which could also scroll the collapsed panel sideways). It waits while another sidebar view covers the Explorer (those rows have no layout) and applies each request once. - `vault.revealPath()` also expands the Explorer section that holds the file, so "Reveal in tree" works from a collapsed section too. ## 17. File operations in the Explorer, with link updating (added 2026-10-14) Like a JetBrains IDE: the Explorer can create, rename, move and delete files and folders, and keep links working. - **Operations**: New file / New folder (Ctrl+N, §3), Rename (F2, inline), Move (drag and drop inside the tree, with a drop-target highlight and auto-expand on hover), Delete (Del; to the OS recycle bin, with a confirm naming the count). Multi-select (Ctrl/Shift+click) for move and delete. Same rules for images and other files. - **Link updating** on rename/move: rewrite (a) links in other Markdown files that point to the moved paths, and (b) relative links and images inside the moved Markdown files. Anchors (`#section`) and the link's text are kept; only the target span of each link is rewritten (by sourcepos), every other byte stays as is. - **Preview first**: "Update 7 links in 4 files?" with the list of changes; [Apply] [Move without updating] [Cancel]. Setting "Update links when moving files: Ask | Always | Never" (default Ask). - **Undo**: Ctrl+Z in the Explorer (and a toast "Moved 2 files, updated 7 links [Undo]") reverts the whole operation: the move and every rewrite, as long as those files did not change since. - **Safety**: a file changed on disk between preview and apply (e.g. an agent writing it) is skipped and reported; a file open with unsaved edits gets the rewrite applied to its buffer, not the disk. Moves outside the project are refused. The live feed shows the operation as one grouped row ("Moved 2 files, 7 links updated"), not a burst. ## Release split (decided with the user, 2026-10-14) - **v0.2**, the "Markdown IDE" release: tags ✅, Explorer filter ✅, reading width ✅, auto-select in the tree ✅, outline, core editor (§3), file operations with link updating (§17). - **v0.3**: Search everywhere (Ctrl+T: files, sections, tags and commands in one box; semantic results join it), unread markers (§4), clickable code references (§5), "Open with PerMark" in the file manager (§14), semantic search.

# PerMark MVP: wireframes, flows, keyboard, components

Scope: the **MVP section of `plan.md`** only. Visual reference: `mockup.html` (IDE mode, light/dark).
Tokens and type come from the design system. Lucide icons only.

Legend: `[@]` copy reference, `[E]` open in external editor (**the slot "Edit" takes in v0.2**), `[:]` more menu,
`M A U D R C` git badges, `o` folder roll-up dot, `++` changed block (glow, then gutter bar), `--` removed-block marker,
`(o)` live dot, `[x]`/`[ ]` toggles, `[...]` buttons. All text in the UI is English and tool-agnostic, via `t()`.

## 1. Welcome

```
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                                              |
|                                  PerMark                                   |
|                 Read, navigate and follow your Markdown docs.                |
|                                                                              |
|        [ Open folder...          Ctrl+O ]   [ Open file...    Ctrl+Shift+O ] |
|                                                                              |
|        RECENT FOLDERS                                                        |
|      > permark-docs     F:\AIProjects\Markdown              2 hours ago    |
|        big-repo           F:\work\big-repo                      yesterday    |
|        notes              D:\old\notes  (not found)                 [Remove]    |
|                                                                              |
|        Drop a folder or a .md file anywhere to open it.                      |
|                                                                              |
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
- Recent list: Up/Down + Enter opens; `Del` removes. Missing folders are dimmed with "(not found)" and only offer Remove.
- **Drag over**: the window gets a 2px dashed accent outline and one centered line, "Drop to open. Folder: IDE mode.
  File: Simple mode." Several items dropped: "Drop one folder or one file."
- Empty recents: the list is replaced by "No recent folders yet." Loading after a pick: spinner in the button (no screen swap
  until `openVault` resolves; error shows inline under the buttons, e.g. "Can't open F:\x: access denied").

## 2. IDE mode (main)

```
+---+------------------------+--------------------------------------------------+--------------------------+
|[F]| EXPLORER           [:] | <- ->  docs / specs / live-feed.md  M  [@][E][:] | LIVE CHANGES    o active |
|   | v permark-docs       |--------------------------------------------------| [x] Docs only            |
|[S]|   v docs             o |    +----------------------------------------+    |--------------------------|
|   |     v specs          o |    | status: draft   updated: 2026-10-13    |    | M live-feed.md      12s  |
|[L]|      [live-feed.md]  M |    | tags: feed, watcher                    |    |   docs/specs  3 saves    |
|   |       watcher.md       |    +----------------------------------------+    | + ui-notes.md       1m   |
|   |     v research       o |                                                  |   @wt feature-ui         |
|   |       storage.md     U |    Live changes feed                             | - old-notes.md      3m   |
|   |       watchers.md    M |    ==========================================    |   docs  removed          |
|   |     > design           |    The feed lists every file the watcher sees,   | > checkout: 143 files 8m |
|   |   README.md            |    keyed by path and updated in place.           |                          |
|   |   plan.md            M |                                                  | v SINCE LAST VISIT  (5)  |
|   |                        |  ++Bursts of saves collapse into one entry.      |   since Mon 18:40        |
|   | WORKTREES              |  ++and never produce more than one toast.        |   docs/specs/            |
|   | > @wt feature-ui       |                                                  |     M live-feed.md       |
|   |   feature/ui           |  -- - - - 1 block removed - - - - - - [show]     |     A watcher.md         |
|   | > @wt fix-links        |                                                  |   docs/research/         |
|   |   fix/links            |    Event model                                   |     M watchers.md        |
|   |                        |    +------------+------------+--------------+    |   (root)                 |
|   |                        |    | Event      | Source     | Grouping     |    |     M plan.md            |
|   |                        |    | modified   | watcher    | by path      |    |                          |
|   |                        |    | checkout   | git        | bulk         |    |                          |
|   |                        |    +------------+------------+--------------+    |                          |
|[T]|                        |    [!] Note: temp files never reach the feed.    |                          |
|[*]|                        |    ...                                           |                          |
+---+------------------------+--------------------------------------------------+--------------------------+
| git: main   5 changed   Since: last visit v              State: Local   Follow [ ]   100%   Normal width |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
**Activity bar**: `[F]` Explorer and `[S]` Search are two views of the sidebar (clicking the active one collapses it),
`[L]` toggles the right panel (shows an accent dot when events arrive while it is hidden), `[T]` theme cycle (system/light/dark), `[*]` settings popover (theme, reading width,
reference template with a live preview). Panels collapse to give the doc the full width; state is saved in the session.

**Tree**: dirs first; badge letter in git color, file name tinted only for `D` (struck) and `C`. Folders show a roll-up dot
(worst state wins: conflicted > deleted > modified > added). Click opens; Enter/Space on keyboard; Left/Right collapse/expand.
The open doc is highlighted and revealed. Worktrees are extra top-level roots with their branch as a muted subline
(no badges inside worktrees in the MVP). Context menu: Copy path, Copy reference, Open in external editor.
`tree-changed` re-fetches the tree, keeping expansion and scroll.

**Doc header**: back/forward (disabled at the ends), breadcrumb (click a segment = reveal that folder in the tree),
git badge, "saved 12s ago" from `modifiedMs`. `[@]` copies `@{path}` (template), `[E]` opens externally, `[:]` holds
Copy path, Reveal in tree, Reading width, Zoom. `encodingNote` shows as a muted chip ("Decoded from UTF-16").

**Live changes** (right panel): one row per path (`fs-change` updates in place and moves it to the top), kind dot
(+ created, M modified, - removed, R renamed "from x"), folder or `@wt <name>` label, save count, relative time
(refreshed every 30s). Click opens the doc (removed: opens the tombstone). The open doc's row has an accent bar.
Header status: "(o) active" while events arrived in the last 30s, else "idle 4m"; nothing pulses with reduced motion.
"Docs only" (default on) hides non-Markdown files; the count of hidden ones shows as "+9 other files".
**Since last visit**: grouped by folder, collapsible, click opens. Header names the baseline time.

**Status bar**: branch (or `detached a1b2c3d`, `no commits yet`), change count, baseline menu ("Since: last visit" /
"Since: last commit", each item shows its time or short oid), Follow toggle, zoom (click resets), width toggle.
**Repo-state banner** (merge/rebase/cherry-pick/revert/bisect) sits under the doc header:
"Rebase in progress. Files may change quickly; large batches are grouped in the feed." with Dismiss (until state changes).
The status bar keeps a small "REBASING" chip after dismissal.

**On file change**: open doc changed on disk → re-render, scroll anchored to the first visible block, LCS diff marks
blocks (§7). Another doc changed → feed row + toast (§8). Tree badges update from `git-status-changed` without flicker.

### Project state: Local (default) or `.permark/` (opt-in)
By default nothing is written to the project. The Explorer `[:]` menu (Collapse all, Reveal open doc, **Initialize
PerMark in this project...**) and the status bar item `State: Local` (click opens a menu with the same command) start it.
A one-time hint sits at the foot of Since last visit: "Keep settings with the project? Initialize .permark/ [x]";
it never returns once dismissed or used (stored globally). After init the item reads `State: .permark`.

```
+------------------------------------------------------------+
| Initialize PerMark in this project?                      |
|                                                            |
| PerMark will create .permark/ in permark-docs:       |
|   config.toml   shared settings, safe to commit            |
|   cache/        search index (gitignored)                  |
|   local/        your session and last visit (gitignored)   |
|                                                            |
| Your current state moves there. Delete the folder to undo. |
|                                                            |
|                                     [Cancel]  [Initialize] |
+------------------------------------------------------------+
```
Modal, focus on Initialize, Esc cancels. Also writes `.permark/.gitignore` (`cache/`, `local/`). On failure (read-only
folder): inline error in the dialog, state stays Local. No undo command in the MVP; deleting the folder falls back to Local.

## 3. Simple mode (a single file was opened)

## 12. Flows

**Open project**
1. Launch (or `permark <path>`); a folder argument skips Welcome.
2. Welcome: pick a recent (Enter) or Open folder (Ctrl+O), or drop a folder.
3. Tree, git snapshot and Since last visit load in parallel; the last doc and scroll are restored from the session.

**Morning catch-up**
1. Open the project; Since last visit is expanded on the right, with its baseline time.
2. Click the first file; it opens (changes vs baseline inside the page are v0.2).
3. Optionally switch the status bar to "Since: last commit" to see only uncommitted work.

**Follow an agent live**
1. Start the agent in a terminal; keep PerMark next to it.
2. Toggle Follow (Ctrl+Shift+L or the status bar).
3. Each save of a doc opens it and scrolls to the changed block; glow fades, gutter bars remain.
4. Read freely: selecting text or opening find pauses jumps; the toast still reports changes.
5. Feed shows "idle 2m" when the agent stops; F7 / Shift+F7 walks the changed blocks.

**Burst of 15 files**
1. Agent saves 6 docs + 9 other files in 40s.
2. Feed (Docs only) shows 6 rows, "+9 other files"; one toast counts up "6 docs changed".
3. Follow, if on, dwells: one jump per 3s, docs only. A checkout during this is one bulk row, no jump.
4. Click rows in order (or Ctrl+P, empty query) to review each doc.

**Find information** ("where are the character descriptions?")
1. Ctrl+Shift+F, type `character descriptions`; results group by file with section breadcrumbs.
2. Down to the best hit (`lore.md > Characters > Aria`), Enter: the doc opens at that section, tinted briefly,
   terms highlighted and the find bar ready.
3. Down + Enter for the next hit, or Enter in the find bar to step through terms in this doc.
4. Knows the file name instead: Ctrl+P. Follow links; Alt+Left to return.

**Send feedback to the AI**
1. Select the passage; the popover appears.
2. Copy with reference (or Ctrl+Alt+C); paste in the agent's terminal and type the request.
3. Without a selection, `[@]` or Ctrl+Alt+C copies just the reference `@docs/x.md`.

## 14. Component inventory (12 components)

| Component | States | Used in |
|---|---|---|
| IconButton | default, hover, pressed, toggled-on, focus, disabled, "done" check (1.2s) | everywhere |
| TreeItem | file/dir/worktree root; hover, selected (open doc), focus, collapsed/expanded, badge M/A/U/D/R/C, roll-up dot, live-updated (badge fades in 180ms) | sidebar |
| DocHeader | nav enabled/disabled, badge, saved-time, encoding chip, loading bar, follow chip | IDE, Simple |
| DocView | rendering, rendered, changed (glow -> gutter), removed marker (closed/open), tombstone (dimmed), find marks | main |
| Notice | empty state (icon, title, text, actions); banner info/warning/error, dismissible | doc, panel |
| SectionHeader | expanded/collapsed, count, action slot | right panel, tree |
| FeedRow | kind created/modified/removed/renamed, current doc, worktree label, saves count, hover, focus; bulk collapsed/expanded | right panel, quick open |
| StatusItem | text, menu, toggle on/off, warning | status bar |

Frontmatter card and alerts are pure CSS in `markdown.css`, not components.

## 15. Flags: spec conflicts and MVP cuts

- **Section search moved into the MVP** (was v0.2 in `plan.md`; it also adds `search`/`index-progress` to the contract).
  It is the largest UI addition here (~20 min UI on top of the Rust index). Simpler variant if time runs out: flat hit
  list (no file grouping), open at the heading without the find-bar pre-fill.
- **`.permark/` reverses decision N11** ("state never in the repo") for users who opt in. Kept safe by: opt-in only,
  `cache/` and `local/` gitignored. Agents may read `config.toml`; keep it small and documented.
- **No command palette** in the MVP, so "Initialize PerMark" lives in the Explorer menu and the `State:` status item;
  it joins Ctrl+K in v0.2.

- **No tabs** in the MVP (design system layout says "tabs + doc"): one doc plus history. Tabs: v0.2.
- **Right panel has no Outline** in the MVP (design system says "outline / live changes"); the header reserves a
  segmented switch "Changes | Outline" for v0.2.
- **Ctrl+K command palette** is in the design system principles but not in MVP scope: reserved, unbound.
- **Git colors in light theme**: `#d29922` and `#3fb950` fail AA as text on white. Badge letters use darker variants
  in light theme (`#9a6700`, `#1a7f37`, `#cf222e`, `#8250df`); dots and dark theme keep the spec values.
- **Find highlight** uses a neutral `--mark` token, because the accent means "live change" and must not be overloaded.
- **Contract gaps**: `ChangedSince.files` has no time, so Since last visit is grouped by folder, sorted by name;
  adding `mtimeMs` enables newest-first (small Rust change, recommended). For bulk, the feed needs `changes` filled
  (capped) to list files; otherwise the expanded row only shows the count.
- Additions beyond the spec, all small: gutter bar after the glow, F7 next change, "idle" indicator, Docs-only toggle,
  coalesced toast, Follow skipped during selection/find, auto-open README. Cut any of them first if time runs short.
- Too big for the MVP, deferred: per-list-item diff, image viewer for binary images, "Show as plain text" for too-large
  files, opening another project in a new process from inside the app, styling broken links before they are clicked.

## Addendum (user validation, 2026-10-13): collapsible side panels
- Left panel (Explorer/Search) and right panel (Live changes / Since last visit) can each be **collapsed and expanded**:
  Ctrl+B (left), Ctrl+Alt+B (right), a collapse chevron in each panel header, and clicking the active activity-bar icon toggles the left panel.
- Both are resizable by dragging their inner edge (min 200 px, max 480 px); double-click the edge resets the width.
- Open/closed state and widths persist per project (SessionState). With both collapsed, the doc gets the full width (focus reading);
  the status bar shows small toggle buttons so a collapsed panel is always recoverable.
- Collapse/expand animates 150 ms (instant with prefers-reduced-motion).

# Reading width

Text reads best in a column of about seventy characters, so paragraphs, lists, headings and quotes stay at the measure. Tables, code, diagrams, formulas and pictures often need more room than that, and they are allowed to take it.

## A table that needs room

| Event | Source | Debounce | Grouping | Feed row | Toast | Follow | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| created | file watcher | 150 ms | by path | new entry | yes | yes | A new file is a changed file. |
| modified | file watcher | 150 ms | by path | updated in place | yes | yes | Twelve saves stay one row. |
| removed | file watcher | 150 ms | by path | kept, struck through | yes | no | The row stays until the next scan. |
| checkout | git operation | none | one bulk batch | one collapsed row | no | no | Never produces a toast or a jump. |

A narrow table stays at the measure, because its content does not need more.

| Mode | Width |
| --- | --- |
| Comfortable | 760 px |
| Wide | 1100 px |
| Full | the pane |

## A long line of code

```ts
const summary = events.filter((event) => event.kind !== 'removed').map((event) => ({ path: event.path, at: event.atMs, group: groupOf(event), hidden: isHiddenByFilter(event.path) })).sort((a, b) => b.at - a.at);
```

Short code stays at the measure too.

```ts
const answer = 42;
```

## A diagram

```mermaid
graph LR
  Watcher[File watcher] --> Debounce[Debounce 150 ms] --> Group[Group by path] --> Reconcile[Reconcile with disk] --> Feed[Feed row] --> Toast[Toast] --> Follow[Follow jump] --> Outline[Outline update]
```

## A formula

$$S_n = \sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{(-1)^{k+1}}{k} \cdot \left(\frac{a_k + b_k + c_k + d_k + e_k + f_k + g_k + h_k + i_k + j_k + l_k + m_k}{\sqrt{1 + x_k^2 + y_k^2 + z_k^2}}\right) + \int_0^\infty \frac{e^{-t}}{1 + t^2}\,dt$$

## A wide picture

![An image 1000 px wide](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%22http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%22%20width%3D%221000%22%20height%3D%22160%22%20viewBox%3D%220%200%201000%20160%22%3E%3Crect%20width%3D%221000%22%20height%3D%22160%22%20rx%3D%2212%22%20fill%3D%22%23e8ecff%22%2F%3E%3Crect%20x%3D%2220%22%20y%3D%2220%22%20width%3D%22960%22%20height%3D%22120%22%20rx%3D%228%22%20fill%3D%22none%22%20stroke%3D%22%234f6bed%22%20stroke-width%3D%222%22%20stroke-dasharray%3D%228%206%22%2F%3E%3Ctext%20x%3D%22500%22%20y%3D%2288%22%20text-anchor%3D%22middle%22%20font-family%3D%22sans-serif%22%20font-size%3D%2222%22%20fill%3D%22%234f6bed%22%3EAn%20image%201000%20px%20wide%3C%2Ftext%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E)

--- status: Draft owner: planning-agent updated: 2026-10-13 tags: feed, watcher --- # Live changes feed The feed answers one question: *what changed while I was looking elsewhere?* It lists every file the watcher reports, keyed by path, so a file saved twelve times stays one entry that moves back to the top. > [!NOTE] > Temporary files (`*.tmp`, `~$*`, swap files) and build folders never reach the feed. The filter runs in the core, before events are batched. ## Event model Events come from two sources. The [file watcher](watcher.md) reports single saves; the git-dir watcher reports operations such as checkout or rebase, which arrive as one bulk batch.[^1] | Event | Source | Feed | Toast | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | created | watcher | new entry | yes | | modified | watcher | updated in place | yes | | removed | watcher | kept, struck through | yes | | checkout | git operation | one collapsed entry | no | ### Sources The file watcher and the git-dir watcher are the only two sources; nothing polls. ### Batches A batch closes after 150 ms of quiet, or after one second at the most. ```ts // One batch per quiet period (150 ms), or at most every second. type FsBatch = { changes: FsChange[]; bulk: null | { count: number; reason: "gitOperation" | "large" | "overflow" }; rescan: boolean; }; ``` ## Grouping Bursts of saves collapse into one entry and **never produce more than one toast**: while a burst lasts, the toast updates its counter in place instead of stacking. Each save shows its own toast, so nothing is missed. Follow mode (Ctrl+Shift+L) opens the latest changed doc at most once every three seconds, and never for a bulk batch. > The feed is only useful if it is quiet. If people stop looking at it, it has failed. > > *Design review, 2026-10-12* ## Pipeline ```mermaid graph LR Watcher[Watcher] --> Aggregator[Aggregator] Aggregator --> Reconcile[Reconcile with disk] Reconcile --> Feed[Feed and toast] ``` ## Rollout - [x] Aggregate events (150 ms quiet, 1 s max) - [x] Reconcile with disk and drop duplicates - [x] Bulk detection for git operations - [ ] Follow dwell: at most one jump every 3 s - [ ] Worktree labels in the feed See [the old spec](../old/spec.md) for the first draft, the [lore notes](../world/lore.md#characters) for naming, or the [cost model](#cost-model) below. ## Cost model Reconciling a batch of $n$ files costs $O(n \log n)$ with the sorted merge. $$\int_0^1 x^2\,dx = \frac{1}{3}$$ A broken formula keeps its source: $\frac{1}{$. ## Notes
Bulk
A batch of more than 200 events, or any git operation.
Burst
Normal saves that arrive within ten seconds of each other.
Why not poll?

Polling wastes battery and misses short-lived files. The native watcher is cheaper and exact.

> [!TIP] > Use F7 to jump between the blocks that just changed. > [!WARNING] > Large checkouts can touch thousands of files; they are grouped on purpose. > [!CAUTION] > Do not edit `.permark/cache` by hand. > [!IMPORTANT] > The feed is keyed by path: renames move the entry, they do not duplicate it. The pipeline in one picture: ![Pipeline diagram](../images/pipeline.svg) H2O and E = mc2, plus ~~strikethrough~~ and an autolink: [https://example.com/feed](https://example.com/feed). [^1]: Git operations are detected from the git directory, not from the file events.

# Watcher

The watcher turns raw file events into batches for the [feed](live-feed.md#event-model). See also the [research notes](../research/watchers.md).

## Debounce

Events are held for 150 ms of quiet, with a hard limit of one second, then reconciled with the disk.

```rust
fn flush(&mut self) -> Vec<FsChange> {
    // reconcile with disk: stat + hash, drop duplicates
    self.pending.drain().filter(|c| c.changed()).collect()
}
```

## Limits

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| quiet period | 150 ms |
| max wait | 1 s |
| bulk threshold | 200 events |

Notes on the people and places of the series. Keep this file the single source of truth.

## Characters

Character notes: tall, quiet, a cartographer who trusts maps more than people. Her descriptions change per book as she ages.

Aria carries a brass compass. Physical **descriptions** must stay consistent with book one: grey eyes, a scar over the left brow.

The character sheet lists his scars in order. Keep descriptions short; the narrator never describes him twice in one chapter.

## World

The coast is mapped in three layers: the harbor charts, the inland roads and the old tunnels. Each layer has its own style guide.

Magic costs memory. Every spell removes one concrete detail from the caster's past, which is why descriptions of old places grow vague.
